findings.evidence: finPermPartition_parts (line 87) and finPermPartition_eq_iff (line 94) characterize it; permConjClassPartition uses it through Quotient.lift, not defeq.
findings.fix: Drop @[expose] from finPermPartition; finPermPartition_parts is a same-module rfl and stays valid.
findings.issue: finPermPartition is @[expose] but every consumer uses finPermPartition_parts (a Nat.Partition is fixed by its parts via ext); no module unfolds the body, so the expose leaks the implementation for no benefit.

findings.evidence: Lines 50-77 provide forward and inverse simp lemmas covering the interface.
findings.fix: Drop @[expose] from partitionEquivYoungDiagram (noncomputable, so expose only enables defeq unfolding, which the characteristic lemmas make unnecessary).
findings.issue: partitionEquivYoungDiagram is @[expose] though fully characterized by partitionEquivYoungDiagram_apply_coe/_apply_rowLens/_symm_apply_parts; downstream should never unfold it.

findings.evidence: equivSortedParts is noncomputable, so expose only affects unfolding; equivSortedParts_apply_parts (line 47) already gives the forward map without exposing the body.
findings.fix: Reprove partitionEquivYoungDiagram_apply_coe via Equiv.trans_apply and equivSortedParts_apply_parts instead of bare rfl (use `(rfl)` if a defeq step remains), then drop @[expose] from equivSortedParts.
findings.issue: equivSortedParts is @[expose] solely so the cross-module proof partitionEquivYoungDiagram_apply_coe := rfl (Partitions.lean:54) can reduce through its toFun — a body exposed to compensate for proving a characteristic lemma by defeq.

summary: The characteristic API is complete and correctly annotated, but three definitions carry unnecessary @[expose]. finPermPartition and partitionEquivYoungDiagram are fully characterized by their simp lemmas, and equivSortedParts is exposed only to make a cross-module `:= rfl` proof go through.
